sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Takakia ceratophylla is a minute moss that forms dense green mats on moist, shaded rock and soil in cold mountain habitats. Leafy shoots are about 0.5–2 cm tall; its leaves are deeply divided into narrow finger-like lobes, as shown in the plate.

sections.title: Reproduction
sections.text: Sporophytes are infrequent. When present, the small capsule is borne on a short stalk and matures in late summer to early autumn. The species is known from scattered sites in Asia and the Aleutian Islands.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: No reliable food use or species-specific toxicity information was found; it is a tiny wild moss, not a documented food plant.
